summary.title: Negotiate the right deal with suppliers
summary.one_liner: You learn how to set negotiation objectives, assess supplier leverage, use common price tactics, and lock in a written contract with protective terms.
keywords: how to negotiate a good deal
takeaways: Define your priorities (price, delivery, quality, payment terms, lifetime cost) and decide what you will and won't concede before negotiating.
Your bargaining power depends on how much the supplier needs your business; research the supplier's market position and order book.
Negotiate with staff who have authority, match seniority, and never accept the first offer; ask what else is included at the price.
Do due diligence first: credit-check the supplier and get references from other customers.
Get a written contract covering price, payment terms, delivery, ownership until paid, liability limits, after-sales service, penalties and exit or dispute procedures.
summary.summary: This UK/Québec business guide, adapted by Info entrepreneurs from Business Link UK material, explains how to negotiate supplier deals beyond just price, including delivery, payment terms and quality. It covers planning in writing, assessing your bargaining power against the supplier's need for your business, and using tactics such as making a low counter-offer and exposing ongoing costs. It then advises on due diligence (credit checks and references) and on drafting a signed written contract with protective clauses. The page also includes a general disclaimer that the information is not legal advice.
